Change c0103. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. IV; 1831 Ch. V.

Context before (unchanged): The porter opened the gates of the court, which had that night been my asylum, and I issued into the streets, pacing them with quick steps, as if I sought to avoid the wretch whom I feared every turning of the street would present to my view.

1818 text: I did not dare return to the apartment which I inhabited, but felt impelled to hurry on, although wetted by the rain, which poured from a black and comfortless sky.

1831 text: I did not dare return to the apartment which I inhabited, but felt impelled to hurry on, although drenched by the rain which poured from a black and comfortless sky.

Diff: I did not dare return to the apartment which I inhabited, but felt impelled to hurry on, although [-wetted-] {+drenched+} by the rain [-,-] which poured from a black and comfortless sky.

Context after (unchanged): I continued walking in this manner for some time, endeavouring, by bodily exercise, to ease the load that weighed upon my mind.

result.rationale: Replaces "wetted" with "drenched" and drops a comma before "which"; a synonym swap that keeps the same meaning and imagery of rain.
